name: Career Type
subtitle: Career and Interest Type
instructions: Rate how much you enjoy or are genuinely interested in each activity, from 1 (Strongly dislike) to 5 (Strongly like). These are about interest, not skill. Go with your gut.

questions.text: Building or repairing something with your hands, a shelf, a machine, a piece of furniture, and seeing it come together properly.
Working with tools, machinery, or technical equipment as a regular part of your day.
Operating heavy or specialized equipment, vehicles, industrial machines, or complex physical systems.
Working outside with plants, animals, land, or the natural environment in some capacity.
Figuring out what is wrong with an engine, an appliance, or an electronic device and fixing it.
Taking a blueprint, a plan, or a set of specifications and turning it into something physical.
Work that is primarily physical and hands on, rather than desk based or screen based.
Working with your hands to construct, assemble, or maintain physical systems where you can see and measure the results directly.
Conducting research to get to the bottom of a difficult or poorly understood problem.
Analyzing data or results to find patterns that explain what is actually going on.
Reading and thinking carefully about abstract or complex ideas over an extended period.
Developing theories or frameworks that explain why things work the way they do.
Working in a lab or investigative setting, studying something that isn't yet well understood.
Using mathematics or logic to work through real world problems systematically.
Diagnosing why something isn't working by testing hypotheses and narrowing down the cause.
Exploring a question in depth, gathering information, and synthesizing it into a clear and well-supported explanation.
Creating art, music, or writing as a form of genuine personal expression, not just as a task.
Performing in front of others, whether through acting, music, dance, spoken word, or another medium.
Designing things with an aesthetic dimension, graphics, interiors, clothing, environments, or experiences.
Writing fiction, poetry, essays, or other creative forms where the language and form matter as much as the content.
Improvising or making things up as you go, finding the form through the process rather than following a plan.
Having a creative medium through which you express something that is genuinely yours.
Working in an environment that values originality and personal vision over convention and precedent.
Bringing your own aesthetic sense or creative vision to a project, shaping how something looks, sounds, or feels.
Helping people work through something difficult in their personal or emotional life.
Teaching, coaching, or mentoring someone through a process of learning or growth.
Working in healthcare, counseling, education, or social services in some capacity.
Volunteering or contributing time to the wellbeing of a community or a cause.
Facilitating a group, running a workshop, or guiding people through a structured experience.
Advising or guiding people through important decisions in their life or work.
Work where building and maintaining relationships is a core part of what you do, not a side element.
Being the person someone comes to when they need support, guidance, or a thoughtful listener.
Leading a team or managing a project from start to finish and being responsible for the outcome.
Pitching or selling an idea, a product, or a service and persuading people to get behind it.
Negotiating an agreement or influencing a decision through conversation and persuasion.
Starting something new, a business, a project, an initiative, and driving it forward from an early stage.
Taking charge in high pressure situations where someone needs to make decisions quickly.
Competing against others in a context where results are clearly measurable.
Setting ambitious targets and pushing a team or yourself to hit them.
Operating in an environment where you can have real influence over how people, projects, or resources are directed.
Organizing files, records, or information into a precise and reliable system.
Following clear procedures and well established processes in your day to day work.
Working with spreadsheets, databases, or financial records in a careful and methodical way.
Checking work carefully for errors, inconsistencies, or anything that doesn't add up.
Keeping track of many small tasks, details, and deadlines simultaneously without losing the thread.
Working within a clear structure where roles, responsibilities, and expectations are well defined.
Preparing detailed documentation, reports, schedules, or plans that others can rely on.
Maintaining accurate records and systems so that information is always correct, consistent, and easy to find.
